result.title: When Is Smaller Greener? Right-Sizing Language Models for Agentic AI
result.summary: AI agents use large language models (LLMs) to plan and act over multiple steps, yet models are usually compared per call rather than per completed task. This paper asks: which model should an agent use to complete tasks reliably while minimising energy, cost and time? We show that per-call comparisons can be misleading for agentic AI. Because a task succeeds only if all required steps succeed, small differences in per-step reliability can produce large differences in overall task success. Failed attempts also consume resources. We therefore evaluate models using energy, cost and time per successfully completed task, treating the completed task as the functional unit. On this basis, we develop a decision model for choosing LLMs in agentic workflows. The model applies to tasks with binary or graded outcomes and to settings with or without retries. We show that each resource has a crossover task length at which a smaller, less reliable model ceases to be the greener, cheaper or faster option. These crossovers divide tasks into three regimes: for short tasks smaller models are preferred, for long tasks larger models are preferred, and only between these extremes do preferences among objectives matter. We embed these results in a two-stage framework that separates efficiency from preference. A Pareto screen first removes models that are never competitive; a weighted decision is required only when a genuine trade-off remains. A pilot study of 15 open-weight models from five developers, ranging from 0.6B to 27B parameters, on two multi-step agent tasks with measured GPU energy supports the predicted structure. The model with the lowest energy per completed task changes with task length and task type, and observed crossover points generally match those predicted from per-step measurements. These findings provide a practical framework for right-sizing language models in agentic AI.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多步 agent 任务中应如何选择 LLM 规模，主张以「每个成功完成任务」的能耗、成本与时间作为评价单位，提出含交叉任务长度与三区间划分的决策模型，并用 15 个开源模型在两个多步任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按成功完成任务计量成本」与交叉任务长度的思路，可能为 LVR 中动态计算/思考步数的收益—成本权衡及停止决策的评价提供借鉴线索；但论文不涉及视觉或 latent 状态机制，属概念层面的可核查线索。
